title: Kingdom Rush 6 Heroes: All 12 Heroes & Best Pairings
description: Meet all 12 Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis heroes. See each hero’s role, strengths, pairing ideas, and how to choose two heroes for different stages.
searchIntent: Meet all 12 Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis heroes. See each hero’s role, strengths, pairing ideas, and how to choose two heroes for different stages.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Heroes
hero.lead: Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis has 12 heroes, and you field two heroes per stage. Choose a pair that covers different jobs; Classic Mode instead uses one hero.

sections.heading: All 12 Kingdom Rush 6 Heroes
paragraphs: The roster combines familiar champions with new allies. The names below refer to Genesis; a returning character’s role in another Kingdom Rush game does not automatically describe this version. Use the role column as a starting point for choosing a job, then compare the skills available in your current hero setup.

table.caption: All 12 heroes roster
rows: Add magic to a melee pair

sections.heading: How the Two-Hero System Works
paragraphs: A normal stage gives you two hero slots. Think of those slots as two separate responsibilities, rather than simply picking the highest-ranked names. One hero can stay near the main fighting position while the other responds to a route that has less tower coverage. If both heroes are always in the same place, the second slot may be doing less useful work than it could.

Before starting, identify where enemies can reach the exit and which lane your towers are best prepared to handle. Assign the heroes accordingly. Moving a hero away from a difficult fight can be a sensible decision when another unit can hold that position; sending both heroes away at once leaves the original defense exposed. Keep an eye on the whole road rather than only on the largest group of enemies.

subsections.heading: Front-line and protective heroes
paragraphs: Gerald, Malik and Rhodes are useful starting points when looking for a ground defense role. Their purpose in a pair is to help give your damage sources room to work. A durable-looking hero still needs a sensible position; judge the result by whether the road stays controlled, not by whether the hero is standing nearest to every enemy.

subsections.heading: Damage-focused heroes
paragraphs: Ignus brings close-range fire, while Oni offers a melee damage focus. Drakkan is the arcane dragon option for troublesome resistant enemies. Choose a damage partner after deciding how the lane will be held. Damage alone does not answer the question of which unit will keep a ground threat inside the tower coverage.

subsections.heading: Ranged and dragon choices
paragraphs: Bolin, Ashbite and Illiana offer alternatives to a pair built entirely around ground melee. Consider them when you want a second source of pressure while your front line does its job. Do not assume that every ranged or flying hero handles every kind of target identically; read the current skill descriptions before committing to a setup.

subsections.heading: Support and magical coverage
paragraphs: Gemina’s illusions and Zefira’s battlemage identity give you different ways to complement a partner. A support choice makes most sense when you already know what it is supporting. Ask whether your defense needs another body, a magical contribution or coverage in another area, and choose around that need.

sections.heading: How to Build a Strong Hero Pair

subsections.heading: Pair complementary roles
paragraphs: Gerald plus Zefira is a straightforward editorial starting point: a paladin alongside a battlemage. Rhodes plus Gemina is an alternative built around protection and illusions. These are pairing ideas, not guaranteed wins. If a stage already has excellent ground control from towers, a different second hero may do more useful work.

subsections.heading: Cover split lanes
paragraphs: On a split map, decide which hero has a permanent position and which one you will move. A pair that looks powerful at one shared choke may be awkward when the roads never meet. Watch travel and attention costs: a hero you constantly forget to reposition may contribute less than a simpler option you manage consistently.

subsections.heading: Match heroes to the tower loadout
paragraphs: Start with the five selected towers, then ask what those towers leave uncovered. If blocking is already reliable, use a hero slot for another job. If the selected towers mainly deal damage, ground support deserves attention. Use spells as the final layer rather than expecting a single hero to fix every gap.
bullets: Give each hero a clear job.
Avoid choosing both slots for the same weakness.
Change one choice at a time when reviewing a failed defense.

sections.heading: Heroes for Different Game Modes
paragraphs: Hero rules change by mode. The main campaign uses two heroes, Classic Mode uses one, Hero Party uses four with no spells, and Spell Rush removes heroes. A normal two-hero pairing therefore cannot be copied unchanged into every challenge.

In Classic Mode, choose the one hero that complements the original tower lines. In Hero Party, divide responsibilities across the available heroes rather than stacking them without a plan. In Spell Rush, solve problems through tower selection and spell timing; no hero can be held in reserve as an emergency response.

sections.heading: Best Kingdom Rush 6 Heroes
paragraphs: Use our tier list to narrow a choice, then check the stage. Ignus and Drakkan are strong launch-window candidates for a damage-focused slot; Gerald is a clear reference point for a ground anchor. Ease of use matters too: a hero whose job you understand is a better starting choice than a highly ranked hero whose positioning you cannot yet manage. Rankings can vary by stage and loadout.

faq.question: How many heroes are in Kingdom Rush 6?
faq.answer: There are 12 heroes in the launch roster.

faq.question: How many heroes can you use per stage?
faq.answer: The normal campaign uses two heroes. Classic Mode uses one, Hero Party uses four, and Spell Rush uses none.

faq.question: Which heroes are best for beginners?
faq.answer: Start with complementary roles such as Gerald and Zefira, then adapt the pair to your available heroes and stage layout.

faq.question: Who are the Kingdom Rush 6 heroes?
faq.answer: Malik, Bolin, Connor, Drakkan, Gemina, Ignus, Rhodes, Gerald, Zefira, Ashbite, Oni, Illiana.

title: Kingdom Rush 6 Towers: All 15 Towers & Best Uses
description: See all 15 Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis towers, what each tower is built to do, how five-tower loadouts work, and which roles fit different stages.
searchIntent: See all 15 Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis towers, what each tower is built to do, how five-tower loadouts work, and which roles fit different stages.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Towers
hero.lead: Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis has 15 towers, and you bring five towers into battle. Build a loadout around coverage, ground control and the demands of the stage.

sections.heading: All 15 Kingdom Rush 6 Towers
paragraphs: The launch roster contains fifteen named towers. This is the normal Genesis selection, distinct from the original tower lines used in Classic Mode. Roles below describe the kind of contribution to look for; they do not imply that two towers in the same broad category have identical targeting or upgrades.

sections.heading: How the Five-Tower Loadout Works
paragraphs: You select five tower types to take into a normal battle. Five selected types is a loadout limit, not a statement that a map contains only five build positions. Decide which jobs need to be available before entering the stage. A choice that duplicates an existing role uses a slot that could otherwise cover a missing one.

Start with a plan for ordinary ground enemies, a plan for threats your main damage source handles poorly, and a way to keep the road under control. Then use the remaining room for a specialist. The map matters: multiple isolated roads create a different placement problem from a long road that passes several tower positions. Do not assume your previous successful loadout is automatically complete for the next map.

subsections.heading: Ranged coverage
paragraphs: Archer Garrison and Elven Elite Ranger are natural reference points for ranged coverage. Cursed Crossbows adds a dark weapon theme, while Sentry Watchtower emphasizes distant sharpshooting. Check the actual targeting rules before relying on a tower for airborne threats. Range is useful only when the important part of the road passes through it.

subsections.heading: Magic and support
paragraphs: Scholar Mage, Light Priestess, Sunray Master and Arcane Forger offer different magical approaches. Light Priestess combines offense with protection nearby. Do not collapse all these choices into one interchangeable mage slot: support, concentrated attacks and general coverage ask different things of your placement and the other towers around them.

subsections.heading: Blocking and lane control
paragraphs: Knights Order gives a clear barracks reference. Wildcat Huntresses and Ironbark Treant provide alternative ways to shape a ground defense. Put the holding point where the rest of your loadout can exploit it. A strong blocker far away from your damage sources can create a long fight without solving the wave.

subsections.heading: Artillery and specialists
paragraphs: Dwarven Culverin and Royal Catapult are the artillery options to compare. Alchemist Shack uses potions to hinder and hurt, while Gold Prospectors combines fighting with gold generation. Specialist utility must justify the selected slot. Extra resources or control are most useful when the rest of the defense can turn that advantage into a safe road.

sections.heading: How to Build a Balanced Tower Loadout
paragraphs: A balanced selection does not mean putting one of every visual style on the bar. It means having answers to the threats and paths in front of you. Compare physical and magical coverage, whether you can hold ground enemies, and whether the remaining slots help the whole defense rather than simply adding another favorite.

Consider a starting framework with Archer Garrison for ranged fire, Scholar Mage for magic, Knights Order for blocking and Royal Catapult for area pressure. The fifth selection should answer a particular map problem. This is an editorial framework, not a universal preset or a requirement to own a specific tower. Substitute available choices that perform the job you actually need.

Placement and selection are separate decisions. A suitable tower can still be wasted in a poor position. Look for stretches of road where coverage overlaps and where a held group can remain under fire. On divided routes, spending everything around one powerful group of towers may leave the other side with no reliable answer.

steps.heading: Read the route
steps.description: Identify the exits, separate lanes and useful shared fighting positions.

steps.heading: Assign five jobs
steps.description: Check damage coverage, blocking and the reason for each specialist slot.

steps.heading: Review the leak
steps.description: If a run fails, identify the uncovered role before replacing the whole loadout.

sections.heading: Best Towers for Common Situations
paragraphs: Scholar Mage and Royal Catapult are good starting points for a general-purpose damage core in our launch-window rankings. Knights Order becomes especially valuable when a ground holding point is the missing piece. Sentry Watchtower deserves consideration when distant coverage fits the road, while a utility choice needs a stage where its contribution can be put to work.

Avoid reading a lower tier as an instruction never to use that tower. A specialist that solves your specific leak may outperform another damage tower that duplicates what is already working. Keep the rest of the team in mind: heroes and spells can cover a weakness, but depending on an emergency response every time the same threat appears makes the defense harder to manage.

sections.heading: Classic Towers vs Genesis Towers
paragraphs: Classic Mode uses the original Archer, Barracks, Mage and Artillery lines with their original upgrade paths. Its twenty listed names include stages along those paths and final specialists. They are not another twenty choices added to the fifteen-tower Genesis loadout. Use the Classic guide when deciding between those branches, rather than applying a normal-mode tier table directly.

faq.question: How many towers are in Kingdom Rush 6?
faq.answer: The normal Genesis roster has 15 towers.

faq.question: How many towers can you bring into battle?
faq.answer: You select five tower types for a normal loadout.

faq.question: Are Classic Mode towers the same as Genesis towers?
faq.answer: No. Classic Mode uses the four original tower lines and their upgrade paths.

faq.question: What is the best tower?
faq.answer: Scholar Mage and Royal Catapult are strong editorial starting points, but the best choice depends on coverage, placement and the rest of your loadout.

title: Kingdom Rush 6 Tier List: Heroes, Towers & Spells
description: Kingdom Rush 6 tier list for heroes, towers, and spells, with role-based rankings, pairing logic, and clear notes on when each pick works best.
searchIntent: Kingdom Rush 6 tier list for heroes, towers, and spells, with role-based rankings, pairing logic, and clear notes on when each pick works best.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Tier List
hero.lead: This launch-window Kingdom Rush 6 tier list ranks heroes, towers and spells as editorial recommendations. Stage layout, enemy mix and loadout synergy affect every pick’s value.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Tier List at a Glance
paragraphs: S means a strong starting recommendation, A means a good complementary choice, and B means a specialist whose slot needs a clear reason. These letters express editorial priorities for normal campaign planning. They are not damage measurements, a promise of success, or a ranking for every challenge mode.

table.caption: Compact tier overview
rows: Reinforcements; Rain of Fire; Wintersong’s Wrath

sections.heading: Hero Tier List
paragraphs: Choose a hero pair, not two letters in isolation. A ground anchor can make an aggressive partner more practical, and a specialist may solve a particular stage even when a more flexible hero sits above it.

table.caption: Hero tier recommendations
rows: Add magic to a melee pair

subsections.heading: S Tier Heroes
paragraphs: Ignus and Drakkan are our launch-window damage priorities. Pick the one whose role fits the pressure you need to answer, then build the second slot around the remaining job. Choosing both is not automatically better than pairing one with a ground anchor.

subsections.heading: A Tier Heroes
paragraphs: The A group is where complementary choices matter most. Gerald or Rhodes gives a defensive direction; Gemina changes the support plan; Zefira adds a battlemage option. Ashbite is a useful crowd-oriented alternative. These choices can be the more practical answer when the map or your selected towers already covers the S-tier role.

subsections.heading: B Tier and Situational Heroes
paragraphs: Bolin and Connor belong to our situational group. A lower recommendation reflects how specifically we would plan their job, not a claim that they cannot finish the campaign. Give a chosen specialist a position and a partner that lets its contribution matter.

sections.heading: Tower Tier List
paragraphs: Our tower table favors a dependable damage core first, then the blocking and specialist choices that help that core work. Every entry still has to earn one of five selected slots.

subsections.heading: S Tier Towers
paragraphs: Scholar Mage and Royal Catapult offer a straightforward starting damage core. Concentrate their useful coverage around a position where enemies can be held. If the map pulls fights far apart, rethink the placement plan before assuming that selecting both is sufficient.

subsections.heading: A Tier Towers
paragraphs: The A choices fill the practical gaps around your damage core. A barracks choice may be the first addition when the road will not stay controlled. A ranged option may deserve the next slot when your current selection lacks the right coverage. Judge the result as a team rather than five separate towers.

subsections.heading: B Tier and Situational Towers
paragraphs: The B group contains more specific utility and attack plans. Gold Prospectors, for example, needs a defense that can make use of its resource role. A specialist can move up in practical value if it fixes your exact problem, but adding one without a purpose makes the loadout harder to evaluate.

sections.heading: Spell Tier List
paragraphs: Spell rankings here prioritize a simple emergency plan: ground help, immediate damage and control. The spell letters are scenario-based editorial guidance rather than a comparison of cooldowns or damage values.

subsections.heading: S Tier Spells
paragraphs: Reinforcements, Rain of Fire and Wintersong’s Wrath form an easy-to-understand role framework. Ground help, damage and control answer different problems. That distinction is why we recommend starting with their jobs rather than three spells chosen only for visual impact.

subsections.heading: A Tier Spells
paragraphs: Teleportation Sigil, Thunder Zapper, Ace Musketeers and Aspect of Sol are alternatives when displacement, lightning or summoned assistance better fits the stage. Compare the gap they solve with the spell you would remove. More options on paper do not guarantee a clearer response during a busy wave.

subsections.heading: B Tier and Situational Spells
paragraphs: Royal Edict and Soaring Shop are situational recommendations here. Read their current in-game descriptions and give them a concrete role before exchanging a familiar emergency tool. Their position reflects our preference for a simple first loadout, not an exact power calculation.

sections.heading: How We Rank Kingdom Rush 6 Picks
paragraphs: We prioritize versatility, lane coverage, reliability, synergy and opportunity cost. A choice ranks well when it fits a clear job in a five-tower, two-hero, three-spell team without forcing the remaining slots to repair too many weaknesses. Ease of use also matters: a powerful idea that demands more attention than you can give it may not be your most reliable option.

Launch-window rankings are a starting framework. Different guides emphasize different combinations and can place the same hero in different tiers. Our table uses that uncertainty to favor roles and adaptable decisions. It does not claim a community vote or a mathematical consensus. Read the reason column as closely as the letter.

sections.heading: The Best Loadout Depends on the Stage
paragraphs: A shared choke rewards a different team from several separated lanes. A defensive specialist can be more valuable when the route lacks a safe holding point; additional damage can matter more once control is stable. Change one role after a failed attempt, then assess whether it solved the actual leak. For Classic Mode, start again from that mode’s restricted roster rather than importing this entire table.

faq.question: Who is the best hero in Kingdom Rush 6?
faq.answer: Ignus and Drakkan are our S-tier starting recommendations. The best partner depends on your stage and tower coverage.

faq.question: What is the best tower?
faq.answer: Scholar Mage and Royal Catapult lead our normal-campaign recommendations, with complementary blocking and coverage still required.

faq.question: What are the best spells?
faq.answer: We prioritize Reinforcements, Rain of Fire and Wintersong’s Wrath as a clear help, damage and control framework.

faq.question: Does the tier list change by stage?
faq.answer: Yes. Stage layout, enemy mix, available upgrades and loadout synergy can change a pick’s practical value.

faq.question: How many choices are in a normal loadout?
faq.answer: Five towers, two heroes and three spells.

title: Kingdom Rush 6 Classic Mode: Rules & Towers
description: Learn Kingdom Rush 6 Classic Mode rules: one hero, four original tower lines, Rain of Fire and Reinforcements, plus how the mode changes strategy.
searchIntent: Learn Kingdom Rush 6 Classic Mode rules: one hero, four original tower lines, Rain of Fire and Reinforcements, plus how the mode changes strategy.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Classic Mode
hero.lead: Kingdom Rush 6 Classic Mode uses one hero, classic towers only, and just Rain of Fire and Reinforcements. Its four original tower lines are Archer, Barracks, Mage and Artillery.

sections.heading: What Is Classic Mode in Kingdom Rush 6?
paragraphs: Classic Mode, also called Classic Rush, revisits Genesis campaign stages with the original Kingdom Rush arsenal. The point is to solve the map with a different set of tools. It is a mode within Genesis rather than a separate purchase or a separate game in this guide’s navigation.

The familiar four tower lines return with their original upgrade paths. At the same time, you have only one hero and the two iconic spells. That smaller set of choices changes how you prepare a defense. A normal Genesis strategy that relies on two heroes or a specialist tower must be reconsidered before it becomes a Classic strategy.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Classic Mode Rules
paragraphs: The essential restrictions are simple: one hero, classic towers only, and Rain of Fire plus Reinforcements. Do not treat this as a normal loadout with one hero removed. The tower selection and spell tools change too, so the complete plan needs to fit the mode.

sections.heading: All Classic Mode Towers
paragraphs: Each row below is one original tower line. The first three names show the progression along that line; the last two are the final specialist choices. The twenty names are therefore a reference to upgrade paths, not twenty independent loadout slots.

table.caption: Classic tower lines
rows: Archer Tower → Marksmen Tower → Sharpshooter Tower
Militia Barracks → Footmen Barracks → Knights Barracks
Mage Tower → Adept Tower → Wizard Tower
Dwarven Bombardier → Dwarven Artillery → Dwarven Howitzer

subsections.heading: Archer Tower Line
paragraphs: Archer Tower progresses through Marksmen Tower and Sharpshooter Tower, with Rangers Hideout and Musketeer Garrison as specialists. Keep ranged coverage in mind when planning this line. Choose the branch for the position you need it to serve rather than upgrading automatically because it was your favorite in a previous game.

subsections.heading: Barracks Line
paragraphs: Militia Barracks leads through Footmen Barracks and Knights Barracks to Holy Order (Paladins) or Barbarian Hall. The holding point deserves as much attention as the tower itself. Put a ground defense where nearby damage can support it, and consider what happens to that road when your single hero has to move away.

subsections.heading: Mage Tower Line
paragraphs: Mage Tower, Adept Tower and Wizard Tower lead to Arcane Wizard or Sorcerer Mage. Give magical coverage a place in the plan rather than relying on one attack style everywhere. The branch decision should follow the problem at that position and the support already available from other lines.

subsections.heading: Artillery Tower Line
paragraphs: Dwarven Bombardier, Dwarven Artillery and Dwarven Howitzer lead to Tesla x104 or Big Bertha. Think about where groups of ground enemies can remain under fire. An artillery position with little useful road coverage is less attractive than one that works with the rest of the defense.

sections.heading: Classic Mode Spells
paragraphs: Rain of Fire and Reinforcements are the available spells. You cannot simply bring the normal three-spell selection, so make sure your response plan does not depend on Teleportation Sigil or another Genesis option. With only two spells, using one because it is available can leave fewer answers when the road gets busy.

Give each spell a purpose before the stage starts. Reinforcements can be considered when the road needs extra help; Rain of Fire is the damage response. This is a timing framework rather than a fixed cast sequence. Watch what is actually happening in the lane and choose the response that addresses it.

sections.heading: Classic Mode Heroes
paragraphs: You command a single hero. That hero cannot cover every separated road at the same time, so decide which position needs personal support and which ones should stand on their tower layout. If you choose a hero mainly for damage, make sure the classic tower lines supply enough ground control. If you choose a defensive hero, check whether the rest of the plan finishes enemies effectively.

sections.heading: How to Approach Classic Mode
paragraphs: Begin by reading the map without assuming your normal Genesis selections are available. Identify shared firing positions, places where a barracks can hold the road under tower coverage, and routes that need their own support. Then decide where your one hero will spend most of the battle.

Avoid moving the hero merely because a different part of the screen looks busier. Ask whether leaving the current position creates a larger problem. A hero move is most useful when it answers something the towers cannot comfortably handle, while the old position remains stable.

When a run fails, separate selection, placement and timing. If the road was never controlled, changing a final tower branch may not solve the issue. If control was stable but enemies survived too long, reconsider the coverage around that position. If the defense only broke after both spells were used, review the moments when you spent them.

Classic Mode rewards understanding the four lines together. You do not need a different plan for every named tower in the table; you need a coherent set of positions that work with your hero and two spell responses. Use the campaign stage list to identify the map, then review the mode’s restrictions before retrying.

faq.answer: One hero, compared with two in the normal campaign.

faq.answer: Rain of Fire and Reinforcements only.

faq.answer: Archer, Barracks, Mage and Artillery, each with its original progression and final specialists.

faq.answer: These names refer to the classic arsenal mode in Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Map and All 18 Stages
hero.lead: Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis has 18 campaign stages. Follow the complete stage order below, from Linirean Castle to Vez’nan’s Tower, with six boss encounters marked.

sections.heading: All 18 Kingdom Rush 6 Campaign Stages
paragraphs: Use this numbered order to locate your next campaign battle. A boss marker identifies the named encounter on that stage; it does not describe the waves or prescribe a complete battle sequence.

sections.heading: Campaign Progression
paragraphs: The campaign starts at Linirean Castle and ends at Vez’nan’s Tower. The order is a useful reference when you are comparing a guide with your campaign screen, especially when a familiar location name appears in discussion of several Kingdom Rush games. Use the stage number together with the Genesis name so that you are looking at the right battle.

Steam describes three campaign landscapes: the Citadel, the Stormcloud Depths and Arcania. Treat the full campaign as a sequence of changing defense problems, rather than eighteen copies of one road. The stage list tells you where a battle belongs; the route on screen tells you how to prepare your loadout.

Progression is not a reason to replace the entire team after every stage. Keep the roles that still work, and change the choice that answers a new gap. This makes it easier to understand what helped. Swapping both heroes, all five tower choices and all three spells together can leave you with a successful run but little understanding of why it succeeded.

subsections.heading: Early campaign
paragraphs: Stages 1–8 run from Linirean Castle through Fortress of Acaroth. Use these battles to learn a clear division between holding a road, dealing damage and responding with spells. Before the first marked boss stage, check whether your setup works when your heroes are needed in different places rather than side by side.

subsections.heading: Middle campaign
paragraphs: Stages 9–13 run from Path of Peril through Stormcloud Halls. Three marked boss encounters sit in this part of the order. Approach each map separately: a loadout that handled the previous road may need different coverage or a different hero assignment. Keep a simple record of the role that caused a leak rather than guessing from the final result.

subsections.heading: Late campaign
paragraphs: Stages 14–18 begin at Brightwick Town and lead to Vez’nan’s Tower, with Castle Blackburn along the way. Before retrying, inspect the full path and the available building positions. Late progression is a useful moment to review the whole team, but the most effective change can still be one carefully chosen slot.

sections.heading: Boss Stages in the Campaign
paragraphs: The six marked encounters are Gor’Thok at stage 8, J.T. at stage 10, Sarelgaz at stage 11, Moglok-Hai at stage 13, Lord Blackburn at stage 15 and Vez’nan at stage 18. The table keeps them attached to their campaign positions so you can locate the battle without navigating to separate boss pages. Boss names appear here as a reference; the surrounding route still needs a complete defense plan.

sections.heading: How to Plan a Stage Loadout
paragraphs: First read the road from entrances to exits. Identify where routes meet, where they stay separate, and which building positions can contribute to more than one fight. A position that looks central on the screen is not necessarily the one with the most useful road coverage.

Next assign a job to every selected tower. The normal loadout gives you five tower types, so duplicates need to earn their place. Check that the plan has a way to control ground enemies, useful damage coverage and a response to threats that the main attack style handles poorly. Choose specialists for a map problem you can name.

Then choose the two heroes around what those towers leave uncovered. Decide which hero stays near the main defense and which one moves when another route needs attention. If you expect both heroes to leave the same position frequently, make sure that position can stand on its tower support.

Finally, choose three spells with distinct jobs. If a spell is meant to save a leak, keep watching the lane where that leak is most likely. Using every emergency response in the same early fight can leave you with no clear answer later. The aim is a repeatable defense, not a memorable single cast.

After a failed attempt, identify where the first problem began. Was the holding point outside useful coverage? Did a separate lane have no hero assigned? Did the team depend on a spell that had already been spent? Fix that cause before changing several unrelated choices.

sections.heading: Game Modes Across the Campaign
paragraphs: Beyond the campaign, Genesis offers Iron Challenge, Blitz Challenge, Hero Party, Spell Rush and Classic Mode. These change the rules of preparation. Hero Party uses four heroes and no spells; Spell Rush removes heroes and emphasizes faster spells. Classic Mode uses one hero and the original tower lines with Rain of Fire and Reinforcements. Recheck the chosen mode before using a normal-campaign loadout as your starting plan.

faq.question: How many campaign stages are in Kingdom Rush 6?
faq.answer: There are 18 campaign stages in the launch campaign.

faq.question: What is the first stage?
faq.answer: Linirean Castle is stage 1.

faq.answer: Vez’nan’s Tower is stage 18.

faq.question: Which stages have bosses?
faq.answer: Stages 8, 10, 11, 13, 15 and 18 have the six marked boss encounters.

faq.question: Does this list include separate stage guides?
faq.answer: The full campaign order is kept on this page. Use the related hero, tower and spell guides to plan a loadout.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Release Date and Platforms
hero.lead: Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis released on September 24, 2026. It is available on Steam for PC, the App Store for iOS, and Google Play for Android. The pre-release Steam demo ended July 6, 2026.

sections.heading: Where to Play Kingdom Rush 6
paragraphs: Use the official store for your platform. The Steam title is Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis TD; the game is also available for iPhone and iPad through the App Store and for Android through Google Play.

subsections.heading: Steam / PC
paragraphs: Open the Steam listing to check current compatibility, system requirements, supported languages and the purchase options shown for your region. The PC listing is the right place to check whether your computer meets the current requirements. A general platform label on a guide cannot replace the store’s operating system and hardware details.

subsections.heading: iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: The App Store listing provides the current device and operating system requirements for iOS. Check those details on the device you intend to use, and read the purchase information before buying. The mobile store’s description and any in-app purchase disclosures apply to that platform; do not assume that the PC package describes every mobile purchase option.

subsections.heading: Android
paragraphs: Use the official Google Play listing from Ironhide Game Studio. Check device compatibility and the purchase information shown in your account’s region. If a listing is unavailable for your device, use the store or publisher’s support information rather than looking for an unofficial installer.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Release Date
paragraphs: Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis released on September 24, 2026. It is already available; the launch date is not a future release window. Genesis is the sixth numbered Kingdom Rush game, even though its story takes players back to earlier events in the kingdom.

When comparing a search result with a store, pay attention to the date and tense of the page. Development announcements naturally discuss wishlists and pre-orders, while a current store page shows the released game. For a purchase decision, use the live store listing and the publisher’s current game page rather than an old announcement.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Price
paragraphs: Pricing may vary by region and platform, and promotions may change. Check the official store for the current price in your currency. This guide does not keep a fixed price or discount because a figure from one storefront can be misleading for a reader using another region or device.

Before confirming a purchase, check exactly what the store is selling. A game listing, a bundle and an optional in-app purchase are different purchase choices. Read the current description and store disclosures so that you understand the selected product. The guide’s launch roster count describes the game’s roster, not a promise about which characters a particular mobile purchase unlocks.

If you are comparing PC and mobile, compare the total purchase you intend to make rather than only the first number on each page. Use the current store’s information about optional purchases and included content. Also consider where you want to play: a lower displayed price is less useful if the device or operating system is not supported.

Keep the currency, region and date together when sharing a price with another player. An introductory offer can expire, and taxes or store account settings can affect what a buyer sees. Reopen the store before buying rather than relying on a price copied into a guide or search snippet.

sections.heading: Is the Kingdom Rush 6 Demo Still Available?
paragraphs: The pre-release Steam demo ended on July 6, 2026. It was a preview ahead of the September launch, not the current full release. Old videos and walkthroughs can still discuss the demo, but that does not mean the same download is still available.

Use the live Steam listing for current purchase and download options. Do not confuse an old demo announcement with a free version of the released game. A guide or trailer can help you understand the style of play, while the official storefront tells you what is available to install now.

sections.heading: What You Get at Launch
paragraphs: The launch lineup is 12 heroes, 15 towers, 9 spells and 18 campaign stages. A normal battle uses two heroes, five selected tower types and three equipped spells. Challenge modes change the rules, and Classic Mode returns to the original four tower lines with one hero and two classic spells.

sections.heading: Before You Choose a Platform
paragraphs: Start with device compatibility, then compare the store’s current purchase details. Check available languages if you plan to play in a particular language, and review the operating system requirements if your computer or phone is older. These details belong to the live storefront because they can change with updates.

If you already play other Kingdom Rush games, make sure the title says Genesis or Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis TD. Alliance, Vengeance and the original Kingdom Rush are separate games. Familiar art or returning characters are not enough to identify the product.

Once you have the game, use the map page to follow the campaign order and the roster pages to understand your choices. You do not need a perfect tier-list team before beginning. A clear plan for towers, heroes and spells is a more useful starting point than trying to reproduce every high-ranked selection at once.

title: Kingdom Rush 6 Spells: All 9 Spells & Best Uses
description: See all 9 Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis spells, what each one does, how three-spell loadouts work, and which spell roles fit different battle situations.
searchIntent: See all 9 Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis spells, what each one does, how three-spell loadouts work, and which spell roles fit different battle situations.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Spells
hero.lead: Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis has 9 spells, and you equip 3 spells for a normal loadout. Classic Mode limits your spell choices to Rain of Fire and Reinforcements.

sections.heading: All 9 Kingdom Rush 6 Spells
paragraphs: These are the nine spell names in the current Genesis lineup. Soaring Shop is the current official-site name. It was called Gnome’s Shop in an earlier official lineup post; older guides may therefore use that name for the shop option.

sections.heading: How the Three-Spell Loadout Works
paragraphs: For a normal loadout, you equip three spells. Select them alongside the five towers and two heroes rather than after choosing an otherwise complete team. A spell slot should have a job you can recognize during the battle: help a ground position, answer a crowded road, or control a dangerous group.

Three spells with overlapping purposes can make the bar look powerful while leaving the same weakness unresolved. If the defense already handles a group comfortably, another response for that same group may be less useful than a tool for the lane where you tend to lose control. Plan the selection around the actual map and the roles already supplied by your towers.

Timing is part of selection. Before starting, decide what situation should make you use each spell. That does not mean following a fixed sequence. It means knowing the problem a spell is meant to answer, so you do not spend an important response simply because its button is available.

subsections.heading: Damage spells
paragraphs: Rain of Fire is the familiar emergency damage option, and Thunder Zapper brings lightning. Use a damage spell when it changes the outcome of the fight, not just when several enemies are visible. A strong defensive position can make a damage response easier to aim at a meaningful group. Exact damage and cooldown values belong to the current in-game descriptions.

subsections.heading: Summon and reinforcement spells
paragraphs: Reinforcements, Ace Musketeers and Aspect of Sol bring assistance onto the battlefield. Consider what that assistance needs to accomplish and where the rest of your defense can support it. A summoned ally and a damage cast are different tools; choose the one that solves the road problem rather than assuming every spell should simply remove enemies instantly.

subsections.heading: Control and utility spells
paragraphs: Teleportation Sigil displaces enemies, while Wintersong’s Wrath freezes and hinders them. They can be considered when you want more time or a different arrangement of enemies for your defense to handle. Royal Edict and Soaring Shop round out the lineup with distinct identities; read their current descriptions when planning a specialist slot instead of guessing their effects from the names.

sections.heading: How to Choose Three Spells
paragraphs: Start by checking the weakest part of your current team. If ground control disappears when the heroes move, a help-oriented spell deserves consideration. If a group remains alive too long inside your coverage, a damage response may fit. If the team needs more time to finish a dangerous group, control may be the missing role.

As an editorial starting framework, compare Reinforcements, Rain of Fire and Wintersong’s Wrath. Their different jobs make the plan easy to understand. You can replace a role when the stage calls for another solution; this is not a claim that those three are always the best available choices.

Give the alternative a specific reason. Teleportation Sigil is worth evaluating when displacement fits your plan, while a summoned ally can fit a defense that needs another body or another source of pressure. The useful question is what the replacement does for the whole team and what you lose by removing the old spell.

Watch how the loadout behaves after a few casts. If you keep spending two spells on the same problem, the permanent tower coverage may need work. Spells can rescue a fight, but using all of them to repeatedly cover one weak position makes other lanes harder to manage. Fix the underlying arrangement as well as reviewing the bar.

sections.heading: Spells in Spell Rush and Classic Mode
paragraphs: Spell Rush removes heroes and gives you faster spells. Your tower and spell choices therefore take on jobs that a normal two-hero team could cover. Plan the permanent positions first, then decide where the spell responses fit; a normal loadout copied without its heroes can leave unexpected gaps.

Classic Mode uses only Rain of Fire and Reinforcements. There is no normal third spell slot to fill with another Genesis choice. A control-heavy normal strategy needs a different plan when that control spell is unavailable. Hero Party goes in the other direction: it uses four heroes and no spells, so a spell recommendation does not apply to that mode.

sections.heading: Best Kingdom Rush 6 Spells
paragraphs: Our tier list favors a clear damage, help and control framework for a first normal loadout. That approach makes it easier to recognize which response a fight needs. A different map, hero pair or tower selection can make another spell a better fit. Read the scenario and role notes rather than treating the ranking as a fixed cast order.

title: Kingdom Rush 6 Enemies: Factions, Bosses & Counters
description: Kingdom Rush 6 enemies guide covering 40+ enemy types, five factions, six boss fights, major threats, and practical counters for different waves.
searchIntent: Kingdom Rush 6 enemies guide covering 40+ enemy types, five factions, six boss fights, major threats, and practical counters for different waves.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Enemies
hero.lead: Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis features 40+ enemies from five factions and six colossal boss fights. This guide covers known enemy types, campaign threats and practical counters, helping you adjust tower damage, hero positions and spell timing to the wave ahead.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Enemies at a Glance
paragraphs: The official enemy count describes the variety across the campaign, rather than the number arriving in a single wave. Your immediate task is smaller: identify which enemies your current defense struggles to damage, which ones escape its coverage and which ones threaten your soldiers.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Enemy Factions
paragraphs: The Shadow Order is a secret society of bandits and assassins hired by Vez’nan. Ironhide introduced these cloaked raiders in Devlog #19, connecting them to the bandits of the original Kingdom Rush. They attack the young kingdom’s construction sites, library and roads.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Enemy List
paragraphs: This known campaign enemy roster brings together early raiders and later threats. Bosses appear in their own section below. Use the names to recognize an encounter, then check the current in-game enemy description before committing gold to a counter; returning names can have different properties in Genesis.

sections.heading: Enemy Types and What They Change

subsections.heading: Armored and magic-resistant enemies
paragraphs: Dark Knight is an armored ground enemy without magic resistance. Magic damage is therefore a sensible answer when physical attacks are making little progress. Put that damage where the enemy spends time under fire; an appropriate damage type still needs enough coverage to finish the target.

Giant Spider has magic resistance in Genesis. Compare physical options when a mage-heavy defense stalls against it. Resistance is a reason to diversify, rather than a reason to discard every mage: the same wave may contain another enemy that your magic tower handles well.

subsections.heading: Flying and fast enemies
paragraphs: Crows fly, move quickly and cannot be stopped by soldiers. A barracks position that holds a ground wave will not close an aerial gap. Check whether the towers, hero attacks and spells covering the flight route can hit air targets; range alone does not guarantee a valid target.

For fast threats, watch where the first effective attack lands. If most of the road is outside useful coverage, a stronger tower near the exit may still be too late. Earlier coverage and a reserve spell give you more chances to deal with a leak.

subsections.heading: Ranged pressure and unreliable blocking
paragraphs: Shadow Archer can attack your units from range. A soldier line may fail because it is taking damage before the main ground group arrives. Support that position with damage coverage, and move a vulnerable hero before the position collapses. Watch the fight rather than treating every blocked enemy as permanently contained.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Boss Fights
paragraphs: The official campaign includes six boss fights. The post-launch boss lineup is Gor’Thok, J.T., Sarelgaz, Moglok-Hai, Lord Blackburn and Vez’nan. These encounters are part of the campaign, not six separate game modes. The map guide helps you follow the stage order without treating every difficult enemy as a boss.

Before a boss attempt, decide how your defense will handle the accompanying wave as well as the large target. If every spell is spent on ordinary enemies just before the boss reaches your strongest position, the encounter can become much harder to recover. Keep track of which part of the attempt failed and adjust that part first.

sections.heading: How to Counter Difficult Enemy Waves
paragraphs: Build a damage position and a holding position that work together. A blocker placed outside useful tower range delays an enemy without solving the kill. Area damage is most useful when several targets remain within its coverage; a narrow line of scattered enemies may need another response.

Use your two heroes to cover different jobs in normal play. Consider who supports the busiest lane and who can respond to another route. Keep a spell ready for the wave’s dangerous moment, rather than spending everything on the first group. Compare the tier list’s role recommendations against the actual enemies on your stage.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Roadmap
hero.lead: Ironhide announced the Kingdom Rush 6: Genesis roadmap on September 28, 2026. A mini-campaign is planned for November and another for December 2026, each adding three stages, one tower, one hero, one spell and a story chapter. More content is planned beyond 2026, with details still to come.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Roadmap at a Glance
paragraphs: The schedule gives two release months and a matching content package for each month. The launch row is the baseline already available; the next two rows show additions, not replacement totals. Use the table to distinguish what you can play now from what is on the way.

sections.heading: November 2026 Mini-Campaign
paragraphs: November brings the first announced mini-campaign: three stages, a tower, a hero and a spell, together with another chapter of the story. The month is the release window. Ironhide’s September announcement does not attach an exact launch day to it.

The three stages are the clearest reason to return if you have finished the launch campaign. They add more battles to learn, while the three new loadout choices give you separate things to compare. A stage count tells you the size of the addition; it does not tell you its enemy mix, path layout or difficulty.

For a useful baseline before the update, note which jobs your current team covers well. You can then evaluate the new tower, hero and spell against specific needs: reliable lane damage, ground support or an emergency response. Their names and abilities will determine those roles when Ironhide reveals them.

sections.heading: December 2026 Mini-Campaign
paragraphs: December is the second announced release window. Its mini-campaign has the same stated content count: three stages, one tower, one hero and one spell, plus a new story chapter. It is a separate addition after the November package.

The matching counts do not mean the two campaigns will play alike. A tower’s attack role, a hero’s skills and a spell’s effect are different questions from how many entries arrive. Those details are needed before making a loadout recommendation or ranking any unrevealed character.

If you play through the November stages first, keep a note of the situations that made you change your team. That gives you a practical starting point for testing December’s additions. Compare a new option in a familiar situation before deciding that it should replace something in every stage.

paragraphs: The projected totals below are simple arithmetic: start with the launch lineup and add three stages, one tower, one hero and one spell for each mini-campaign. They show the combined content if both announced packages arrive as described, rather than a separate promise about every future roster entry.

These totals also leave enemy and boss counts open. Extra stages do not automatically establish an equal number of new bosses or a specific number of new enemy types. Read future campaign reveals for those details instead of deriving them from the stage increase.

sections.heading: What Is Planned Beyond 2026?
paragraphs: Ironhide says more content is planned beyond 2026. The September roadmap does not identify those later releases, their size or their timing. The announced November and December packages therefore remain the concrete schedule to use for your next return to Genesis.

A longer horizon leaves room for later announcements without establishing a particular hero, campaign theme or release month. For now, finish the chapters available to you and use the official news page for the next reveal. Future artwork alone is not enough to identify a playable character or explain a new mechanic.

sections.heading: Mini-Campaigns and Balance Updates
paragraphs: The content roadmap and Patch 1 answer different player questions. The roadmap adds battles and loadout choices in November and December. Patch 1 addresses progression, economy, selected stages and other existing systems. Follow the patch page when you want to know whether a familiar strategy or unlock path is changing.

When returning for a mini-campaign, check both the new content notice and the balance notes. A loadout you remember may feel different after a patch even before you try a new hero or tower. Knowing which change belongs to which announcement makes it easier to decide what to test first.

hero.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Patch 1
hero.lead: Ironhide announced Kingdom Rush 6 Patch 1 on October 1, 2026 and said it would arrive early the following week. As of October 6, the official notice remains a preview. Its focus is progression, unlock costs, selected stages, targeting, Classic Mode, Rain of Fire, artillery, Bolin and bug fixes.

sections.heading: Kingdom Rush 6 Patch 1 Status
paragraphs: Patch 1 is announced, with an expected window of early in the week following the October 1 post. The announcement is still the latest official patch notice on October 6. It gives no exact release day. Ironhide says the live patch will be accompanied by a detailed changelog.

table.caption: Patch 1 release information

Not announced in the current notice

sections.heading: Hero and Spell Leveling Changes
paragraphs: Both heroes and spells are due to level faster, with a stronger catch-up bonus. If you have stayed with an established team because another option is underleveled, this is the part of the preview most relevant to trying a different setup. The announcement does not give an experience multiplier or a new leveling formula.

sections.heading: Tower, Unlock and Economy Changes
paragraphs: The preview reduces the stars required to unlock towers, heroes and spells. It also announces more gold on Casual difficulty. These are separate changes: one affects access to your collection, while the other affects the resources you spend during a stage. The notice does not extend the Casual gold increase to every difficulty.

sections.heading: Stages 3, 7 and 10 Changes
paragraphs: Ironhide identifies stages 3, 7 and 10 for adjustments to tower spots and waves. The preview does not publish the revised layouts or wave compositions. An older walkthrough can still explain the stage’s general goal, but its exact placement sequence may need another look after the update.

The targeting change concerns enemies near the exit: visible enemies on the path should remain valid targets. On a fresh attempt after the update, inspect build positions and routes before repeating an older placement sequence.

sections.heading: Classic Mode Changes
paragraphs: Classic Mode has two announced changes: lower ability costs and fully upgraded starting towers on Impossible. The Impossible rule is specific to that difficulty in Classic Mode. It is not an announcement that every tower in every mode will start at its highest level.

sections.heading: Rain of Fire, Artillery and Bolin Changes
paragraphs: Rain of Fire receives a buff, artillery gets cost adjustments intended to make it easier to build, and Bolin receives a mine placement fix alongside a buff and bug fixes. The preview describes the direction of these changes without specifying new damage values, prices or skill numbers.

Test a changed tool in a familiar stage: check whether artillery fits your opening budget, Rain of Fire finishes a dangerous group, or Bolin’s mines contribute where intended. Familiar waves make the comparison easier to understand.

sections.heading: Bug Fixes and Crash Support
paragraphs: Crash issues are being handled in parallel with the patch work. Ironhide’s October 1 post asks affected players to contact support with details about their setup. Record the stage, the action before the crash and whether it happens repeatedly; those details make the report more useful than a general description of a failed session.

The same notice offers Steam players an open beta to try. In the Steam Library, right-click the game, open Properties, choose Betas and select the open beta if it is available. This is a troubleshooting option from the official notice, not confirmation that stable Patch 1 has launched.

sections.heading: What Is Not Confirmed Yet
paragraphs: Ironhide has not published the final numeric values in the current notice; a detailed changelog is planned with the live patch. Exact unlock thresholds, experience changes, artillery prices and Rain of Fire or Bolin balance numbers are therefore still to come.

Patch 1 is also separate from the November and December mini-campaigns. Use the roadmap for new stages and roster additions, and the patch notice for changes to the game you already own. The preview’s list of adjusted stages does not add three new campaign stages.
